I know this is already merged, but shouldn't `startat` be `startAt`?

> I know this is already merged, but shouldn't `startat` be `startAt`?

If we were starting from scratch, yes, but this is how all the other regex methods spell it, e.g. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.regularexpressions.regex.match?view=net-8.0#system-text-regularexpressions-regex-match(system-string-system-int32), so we're staying consistent with that.

review_comments: I forget, Would this also optimize away capture groups given we don't need them? I was sort of assuming that the implementation here would use EnumerateMatches internally and then just produce the right range from that result.

> Would this also optimize away capture groups given we don't need them?

Yes, or at least it will for non-backtracking, where BoundsRequired avoids the need to do the last pass that handles generating capture information.

> I was sort of assuming that the implementation here would use EnumerateMatches internally and then just produce the right range from that result.

I had that initially, and then hit a snag that caused me to move away from it, but I can't recall what that was now.

would it be unacceptably slow to make this close to max string/max array size? that would catch some place where we inadvertently in future, eg., try to allocate twice as much.
but just a nit, feel free to ignore.
It would need to be outerloop and would need to deal with frequent OOMs. It's a fine suggestion, but I don't think it's worthwhile.

any particular reason to put this -- is it our pattern to put this on every struct that has no particular reason (ie interop) to be laid out sequentially?

(do we have/should we have an analyzer to ensure we have StructLayout on all structs, to be explicit?)

> do we have/should we have an analyzer to ensure we have StructLayout on all structs, to be explicit?

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/64261

> any particular reason to put this

Just to avoid me having to arrange the fields optimally, and just seeing from the list of fields that they're not.

should we have a test that produces more than the ~10 results that the current tests max out at? not sure what bug that would expose, unless perhaps some appalling scaling behavior. but it would be easy to have such a test.
So if I don't set this as the option, does that mean that even when only calling EnumerateSplits I'll be paying a small cost if my pattern contains capture groups?

> So if I don't set this as the option, does that mean that even when only calling EnumerateSplits I'll be paying a small cost if my pattern contains capture groups?

The test is setting this just to increase the number of Split tests that are applicable.

This option will have no impact with NonBacktracking, as EnumerateSplits will always tell the engine to not worry about capture groups. For the other engines, they currently ignore that mode being passed in, so regardless of what operation you call, it's beneficial to not have more capture groups than you need.
this means some tests are being skipped here that are valid tests, but just will have different expected results than for Split? is that losing coverage of any interesting cases?

> is that losing coverage of any interesting cases?

Not really. The only ones exempt are the ones explicitly using named capture groups, and those only exist to test that the captures are included.
